title: Shreyas Iyer's Maiden T20I Ton Powers India to Eight-Wicket Win Over West Indies
excerpt: The India captain's unbeaten 102 off 43 balls — the first T20I hundred by an Indian skipper in a run chase — sealed an eight-wicket win with 32 balls to spare in Lucknow.
body:
• Captain Shreyas Iyer smashed an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls — his maiden T20I century — as India chased down 172 to beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series opener at Lucknow's Ekana Stadium on Tuesday.
  • Iyer became the first India captain to score a T20I hundred in a run chase; the previous best by an Indian skipper batting second was Virat Kohli's 94* against the same opposition in 2019.
  • India won with 32 balls to spare, stretching its T20I winning streak to 10 matches, after debutant Naman Dhir's 3/31 and tight spells from Axar Patel and Kuldeep Yadav bowled West Indies out for 171.
  • The win came barely a day after the T20 squad landed from Japan with the Asian Games men's T20 gold medal. The second T20 is on Friday in Ranchi.

Shreyas Iyer chose the biggest stage to announce himself as India's T20 captain, striking a maiden international century — 102 not out off 43 balls — to power India to a commanding eight-wicket win over the West Indies in the opening T20I at Lucknow on Tuesday. Chasing 172, India raced home in just 14.4 overs to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.

A chase turned into a rout

India's chase wobbled briefly after losing both openers inside four overs. Abhishek Sharma's brisk 10-ball 21 ended when spinner Roston Chase had him caught, and Sanju Samson fell for 11 — caught and bowled by left-arm spinner Akeal Hosein, who was playing his 100th T20 for the West Indies.

What followed was a one-man demolition. Iyer, batting with Ishan Kishan (37 not out off 27), raised his fifty off 28 balls, then shifted into another gear entirely: six sixes in the next 18 balls he faced, including a 24-run assault on Matthew Forde in the 14th over. With eight needed off 36 balls and Iyer on 95, Kishan handed his captain the strike; the hundred arrived with a six, and a single completed the chase.

"Definitely exultant — that's the word I would use today," said player of the match Iyer. "I was actually thinking about getting my first century, and it came through. Dreams do come true. Winning tastes different. Today it was me who finished off the game."

Kishan played the perfect supporting role, later admitting he was happy to keep Iyer on strike once the timing clicked: "I was not in great touch. I wanted him to keep the momentum going."

A captain's record

The hundred carried historical weight. Iyer is the first India captain to reach three figures with a target in front of him in T20Is — Rohit Sharma's three captain's centuries and Suryakumar Yadav's one all came batting first, and the previous highest by an Indian skipper in a chase was Kohli's 94* against West Indies in Hyderabad in 2019. His 237.20 strike rate, with 10 fours and six sixes, made it one of the most destructive innings by an Indian captain.

It was also a homecoming of sorts: Iyer had scored his maiden IPL century at the same Ekana Stadium earlier this year, playing for Punjab Kings against Lucknow Super Giants.

"If we continue with the same mindset, we will be one of the most destructive teams."

— Shreyas Iyer, India captain

Spinners set it up

West Indies were bowled out for 171 in 19.1 overs after India's spinners took control. Debutant Naman Dhir was the story of the innings, bouncing back from being hit for sixes to claim 3/31 with three wickets in successive overs. Axar Patel bowled a double-wicket maiden to end the powerplay and finished with 2/26, while Kuldeep Yadav took two wickets to keep the middle overs tight.

Shai Hope, the West Indies captain, made 52 off 37 balls and Sherfane Rutherford top-scored with 56, but the visitors collapsed from 107 for 3 to 135 for 8 before late hitting pushed them past 170. "I thought we were a little bit too chaotic in the batting," Hope admitted. "When you're playing in India, you got to put runs on the board."

Context

The turnaround was remarkable for its speed. Iyer's squad landed in India on Monday evening with the Asian Games men's T20 gold medal from Japan — while, back home, a completely different India squad led by Shubman Gill had just beaten West Indies 2-1 in the ODI series. The win also extended India's T20I winning streak to 10 matches, underlining the depth of the talent pool across parallel squads.

What's next

The series moves to Ranchi on Friday, October 9, followed by matches in Indore (October 11), Hyderabad (October 14) and Bengaluru (October 17), all starting at 7:00 PM IST. With Iyer's captaincy era off to a flying start and the spinners in ruthless form, West Indies face a steep climb to stay in the series.
